answer_text: Nationalists linked India to the image of Bharat Mata, first imagined by Bankim Chandra Chattopadhyay and later painted by Abanindranath Tagore as a calm, spiritual mother. Bankim’s hymn Vande Mataram was widely sung in the Swadeshi movement, and folk tales were collected so people felt pride in shared culture. Flags also bound people together: Bengal’s Swadeshi tricolour and Gandhi’s Swaraj flag with a spinning wheel were carried in marches as symbols of defiance.
